headline: Explicit force models link filament and cell mechanics to emergent stress patterns across scales
label: Mechanics Driven Cytoskeletal Force Models
summary: Five preprints in one week model how mechanical feedback and force transmission organize structure from the actomyosin cortex to whole tissues.
synthesis: The common thread is explicit mechanical modeling in which force, not only biochemical signaling, organizes structure. At subcellular scale, a discrete actomyosin cortex model reconstructs local surface stress from element forces, tying filament mechanics, turnover and myosin to dynamic load-bearing structures. At cellular scale, the Fourier Contour Cell model links deformability and self-propulsion to bimodal intercellular contact-force distributions. At tissue scale, two models of active elastic tissue show that stress feedback on contractile fibers produces bistable strain responses and orthogonally aligned fiber domains, including around a pressurized lumen. MORPHIOME adds imaging-calibrated multiscale modeling of Drosophila wing disc eversion, resolving a mechanical sequence that includes ECM. The new element is the pairing of feedback-driven patterning theory with calibration to imaging data.
